nodes.title: cv2.rapid: tracking a REAL 3D model (not a hand-typed cube - see 95)
widgets_values:
RAPID (Harris & Stennett 1990) is an edge TRACKER, not a detector. Each frame it samples control points along the model's projected silhouette, searches perpendicular to the contour for the strongest image gradient, and refines the pose by PnP - starting from the previous frame's answer. It needs a starting pose that is already close and small motion between frames.

WHAT THIS GRAPH DOES
1. 'Load 3D (Advanced)' loads the GLB; 'CV Mesh From 3D Model' turns it into pts3d (Nx3) + tris (Mx3). Nothing else in the pack could read a mesh INTO the graph before - the same arrays also feed ICP / PPF / point-cloud normals.
2. Four 'CV Preview 3D (Calibrated Camera)' nodes render the truck over a market photo at four KNOWN camera poses. That is the observation: a textured, shaded render over real clutter, not a wireframe the tracker drew itself. 'Batch Images' stacks the four into one IMAGE batch.
3. Two 'CV Rapid Track (Sequence)' nodes track that batch from the SAME frame-0 pose. TOP lane gets the mesh straight from the file; BOTTOM lane gets it through 'CV Mesh Split Long Edges'.
4. The last frame's tracked pose is projected and compared with the true pose - read the two 'mean error' outputs, and look at the overlay. It draws each lane's SILHOUETTE, which is what cv2.rapid actually aligns: RED is the raw-mesh pose, GREEN the split-mesh pose. There is no line for the truth because the rendered truck IS the truth - a lane is right exactly when its outline hugs the vehicle. (Drawing the full 3624-triangle wireframe instead is an unreadable hairball over a photo; and feeding drawWireframe the SPLIT indices with the ORIGINAL projected points fans garbage lines across the image, because it does not bounds-check tris against pts2d.)

nodes.title: WHY THE SPLIT MATTERS (this is the lesson)
widgets_values:
cv2.rapid's extractControlPoints builds each 3D control point by interpolating LINEARLY between two consecutive silhouette VERTICES, with the blend factor taken from screen-space distance. Between far-apart vertices that is wrong by about L_px^2/(16*fx) in depth - and on this model, at fx=900 and 8 m, the raw mesh puts control points up to 23 px away from their own 3D points. The tracker then fits a corrupted correspondence set and walks away from the truth even when it starts perfectly on it.
Splitting long edges until they are <= 80 px on screen (max_edge = 80 * distance / fx = 0.711) drops that to 0.9 px, for 5960 triangles instead of 3624 and about 14% more tracking time. Rendering at a HIGHER RESOLUTION does not help - the error is geometric, not raster.

nodes.title: KNOBS WORTH TURNING
widgets_values:
- max_edge on 'CV Mesh Split Long Edges': set it to 0 to pass the mesh through untouched and watch the bottom lane become the top one.
- scale on 'CV Rapid Track (Sequence)': the capture-range knob. Prefer it over search_length, which buys range by letting texture edges outvote the silhouette.
- ratio / rmsd outputs: ratio is the fraction of search lines that matched (a health signal); rmsd is the 2D reprojection difference in pixels. Neither is an accuracy measure - a confidently wrong pose scores well.

The GLB must sit in ComfyUI/input/3d/MilkTruck.glb (copy it from example_inputs/, see sources.txt).

nodes.title: USE 1 - MATTE
widgets_values: 1. MATTE. 'CV Rasterize Mesh' takes the whole Bx3x1 pose stack and returns one silhouette MASK per frame plus METRIC camera-space depth. That is rotoscoping for free once the object is tracked - feed it to compositing, inpainting or a depth ControlNet.

nodes.title: USE 2 - OCCLUSION
widgets_values: 2. OCCLUSION. The same node's depth is exactly what 'CV Preview 3D (Calibrated Camera)'.scene_depth wants, so a SECOND copy of the truck (same rotation, pushed 1.6 m left and 3 m back in camera space, so it follows the track) is CUT where the tracked one stands in front of it. The occlusion MASK shows which pixels were removed.

nodes.title: USE 3 - CALLOUTS
widgets_values: 3. CALLOUTS. The anchors are AUTHORED in 'CV Annotate Points On Model': run the graph once, then orbit that node's 3D view and click the surface - a plain orbit viewer, no pose and no lens, because you are pointing at geometry. The picks are in the MODEL's own frame, which is what makes them ride the object. 'CV Annotate Model' then projects them through the tracked pose and compares each one's depth with the rendered surface. Anchors on the far side come back as NaN, and the drawing nodes skip non-finite points - so they vanish while the labels keep their numbers. Filtering them out instead would renumber every caption.

nodes.title: USE 4 - MEASURE
widgets_values: 4. MEASURE. The OTHER way to pick: where lane 3 clicks the model, this one clicks the FOOTAGE, and 'CV Draw 3D Measurement' puts the answer back ON the frame - a dimension line between the two ends, captioned at its midpoint with the distance between the 3D POINTS (a real length in the calibration's units, NOT the pixel span of the line). 'CV Pick Point On Mesh' turns two CLICKED PIXELS into two points in the model's own frame (rasterize -> read the depth under the click -> unproject -> inverse pose), and 'cv2 norm' gives the distance between them in the calibration's units. Swap the literal pixel pairs for an 'CV Annotate Points' node to click them on the image instead. A click that misses the object reads valid=0 rather than inventing a point - which is also why the shipped pixels sit well INSIDE the silhouette.

groups.title: 1. THE MODEL - a real GLB into arrays, the camera, the backdrop, and the split that fixes the control points
2. THE OBSERVATION - the truck rendered over a real photo at four KNOWN poses, batched into one sequence
3. THE TRACK - the same frame-0 pose, two meshes: RAW file vs SPLIT edges
4. SCORE IT - last frame vs truth in pixels, and as silhouettes over the frame (red = raw mesh, blue = split)
5. USE 1 - MATTE: one silhouette mask + metric depth per frame (rotoscoping for free)
6. USE 2 - OCCLUSION: a SECOND copy of the truck, cut where the tracked one stands in front of it
7. USE 3 - CALLOUTS: anchors clicked on the MODEL, projected through the tracked pose
8. USE 4 - MEASURE: two pixels clicked on the FOOTAGE, captioned with the 3D distance
